title: Service heatmap and error-mode signatures for latency and failure classification
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a cross-service observability artifact that classifies and surfaces error-mode signatures (canonical failure categories) and a latency/error heatmap for all inference routes. The goal is to make it trivial for on-call engineers and SREs to identify whether issues are due to client-side timeouts, upstream overload, model runtime faults (OOM, kernel stalls, invalid outputs), network/proxy failures (HTTP/gRPC codes), or platform configuration (autoscale/queue misconfig). Deliverables: 1) a canonical failure_mode label and enrichment rules applied to traces/logs/metrics, 2) a Grafana heatmap that slices services by latency buckets and failure_mode, 3) standard PromQL and logQL queries, 4) runbook snippets for each failure_mode, and 5) rollout plan and PRs for trace instrumentation, metric exports, and dashboard panels.
acceptance_criteria: All inference requests contain failure_mode enrichment in trace/span with one of: client_timeout, overload, model_runtime_error, model_bad_output, transport_error, config_misroute, unknown
Grafana heatmap shows 95th/99th latency per service by failure_mode for last 30m and 24h
Prometheus histograms for response_latency_ms and queue_time_ms instrumented on all services and visible in the dashboard
Log pipeline extracts model_error_code and maps common model stack traces to model_runtime_error or model_bad_output
On-call runbook links open to targeted remediation steps and one-click escalation to model-team when model_runtime_error observed
QA: inject fault scenarios (client slowrecv, GPU OOM, simulated gRPC UNAVAILABLE) and verify dashboards tag and surface the correct failure_mode
implementation_notes: Introduce failure_mode label at the trace-ingestion layer using a deterministic rule set (see design_doc link). This is a shallow enrichment only; avoid blocking request path.
Span annotations to add: failure.mode, failure.code, backend.queue_ms, model.exec_ms, kv_cache.hit
Implement in three parallel PRs: tracing hooks (service libs), log parsers (ingest pipeline), metrics (prometheus exporters). Coordinate rollouts with feature flags.
Prefer rule-based initial classifier (regex + HTTP/gRPC code mapping + latency heuristics) to allow easy audit, then iterate to a small ML classifier if false-positive rate > 10%.
Keep enrichment values small (enum-like) to avoid high cardinality in metrics and dashboards. Use label cardinality guard on ingestion pipeline.
Instrument edge/proxy to report client_api_timeout separately from backend_timeout (helps distinguish client timeouts vs platform backpressure).
tracing_changes: Add span.tag 'failure.mode' with canonical values: client_timeout, overload, model_runtime_error, model_bad_output, transport_error, config_misroute, unknown
Add span.tag 'failure.code' to capture HTTP/gRPC numeric codes or model internal code strings
Emit 'queue_time_ms' and 'backend_time_ms' as span fields for accurate breakdown in traces
Add short stack snapshot field for model runtime exceptions (trimmed to 512 chars) to avoid PII and payload bloat
Sampling: for now continue existing sampling rate but ensure 100% sampling for requests flagged with non-2xx or latency > 5s via dynamic sampler
metrics_schema_changes: response_latency_ms histogram (buckets: [5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2500,5000,10000]) exported from inference service frontends and model backends
queue_time_ms gauge and histogram to capture time spent waiting for GPU or CPU worker
gpu_queue_depth gauge exported from dedicated scheduler
failure_mode_count counter partitioned by failure_mode and service (low-cardinality enforced)
log_schema_changes: Structured log JSON with fields: request_id, route, model, model_version, failure_mode, failure_code, backend_duration_ms, tokens, kv_cache_hit
Parser rules to extract model stack traces and map to model_runtime_error/model_bad_output based on known substrings (OOM, CUDA_ERROR, invalid_tokenization, generation_truncation)
Masking rules to redact user prompt content and PII before storing logs in long-term storage
Enforce a maximum log size for trace-linked logs (64KB) to avoid pipeline OOMs
dashboards: Grafana: service-latency-error-heatmap-v1 (panel: heatmap by service x latency_bucket colored by failure_mode)
Grafana: failure-mode-trend (timeseries of failure_mode_count by service and model)
Grafana: latency-breakdown (stacked bar: queue_time_ms vs model.exec_ms vs network)
Explore: LogQL saved query 'errors_by_failure_mode' linking to raw logs filtered by failure_mode
Kibana: model-error-signatures index view with top stack traces mapped to signature buckets
promql_examples: sum(rate(queue_time_ms_sum[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(queue_time_ms_count[5m])) by (service)  # avg queue time
alerting_updates: Create SLO burn alerts that break down by failure_mode rather than only by HTTP 5xx
New on-call page rule: if model_runtime_error spikes > 5x baseline for 15m, auto-create incident and tag model-team
Add low-latency alert for gpu_queue_depth > threshold for 10m with severity P1
Avoid alert storms by grouping alerts by service and top failure_mode (use alertmanager grouping)
Alert thresholds to be validated in canary environment during rollout
runbook_snippets: client_timeout: verify client RTT and proxy logs, check client retry behavior and rate limits. If client-side, escalate to integrator support.
overload: inspect gpu_queue_depth, autoscaler events, and incoming QPS. Consider increasing autoscale limits or enabling burst capacity.
model_runtime_error: check model-serving logs for OOM/CUDA errors, verify quantization profile used, and review recent model rollouts. If persistent, rollback to previous model version.
transport_error: map HTTP/gRPC codes (429->overload, 503->transport_error or backend_unavailable) and inspect network proxies and regional routing.
config_misroute: validate rollout policies and routing rules; common cause is pinned version mismatch across dedicated pools
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 1 week): merge tracing hooks behind feature flag and enable for 5% traffic; deploy dashboards to team Grafana folder
Phase 2 (validation, 2 weeks): enable log parsers in staging, run fault injection tests, iterate classifier rules
Phase 3 (prod rollout): enable enrichment for 100% traffic, monitor cardinality, adjust label throttling if needed
Rollback plan: disable enrichment feature flag and revert to previous dashboards while keeping metrics intact
qa_plan: Fault injection: simulate GPU OOM, client slowrecv, proxy 503 and confirm heatmap/failure_mode tagging
Cardinality tests: run high QPS synthetic traffic to ensure ingestion pipeline enforces cardinality caps
False positive audit: sample 500 traces over a week and measure rule classifier precision/recall
Performance check: ensure enrichment adds <2ms median overhead to tracing path
